chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar who said:

I said to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him): 'If a pregnant woman is divorced by her husband, then he revokes her, then divorces her again, then revokes her again, then divorces her for the third time,' so he said: 'She becomes definitively divorced from him and is not permissible to him until she marries another husband.' This does not contradict the earlier narrations which contained that the divorce of the pregnant woman is one, because we only mentioned that in the case of the divorce of the Sunnah (revocation during the waiting period). As for the divorce of the waiting period (final divorce), then it is permissible for him to divorce her during the duration of her pregnancy if he has revoked her and had intercourse with her. If it is said: 'How is this possible for you with what has been narrated that when he revokes her, it is not for him to divorce her a second time until she gives birth to what is in her belly?' He narrated that.

key_terms.طَلَاقُ السّنّةِ: Divorce of the Sunnah (revocation during the waiting period)
key_terms.طَلَاقُ العِدّةِ: Divorce of the waiting period (final divorce after intercourse)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the divorce of a pregnant woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) resolves the apparent contradiction between narrations by distinguishing between *talaq al-sunnah* (revocable divorce during the waiting period) and *talaq al-'iddah* (final divorce after consummation), ruling that the latter can occur while the woman is still pregnant. This distinction preserves the validity of earlier reports which specified a single count for the pregnant woman's revocable divorce, while allowing for the finality of divorce post-intercourse. The ruling underscores the precision of Shia jurisprudence in harmonizing seemingly conflicting hadiths through contextual analysis of the marital state.
